paper.title_en: Non-Hermitian Schwinger effect in an imaginary magnetic field
paper.abstract_en: We investigate a non-Hermitian Schwinger effect by analyzing a one-loop effective Lagrangian of scalar and Dirac quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the presence of a real electric field and a parallel imaginary magnetic field. We show that an imaginary magnetic field produces an additional pole family in the integrand of the proper-time representation. Unlike a real magnetic field, an imaginary magnetic field can generate a nonzero imaginary part of the effective Lagrangian even in the absence of an electric field. The interplay between the two fields leads to nontrivial phenomena, such as a cancellation mechanism between the contributions of two fields. We also point out that when the ratio of two field strengths is rational, some poles among the two families coincide, and a careful treatment of double poles is required. By further examining the complex Landau-level structure of the electric-pole contribution, we find that the field dependence of the vacuum decay rate from each Landau level exhibits a sinusoidal-like behavior, and their sum determines the overall field dependence. Our results clarify the analytic structure of the QED effective Lagrangian in imaginary magnetic backgrounds and provide a basis for investigating its relation to non-Hermitian phenomena in the QED vacuum.
